final_proof:
Let \(v_p\) be the normalized \(p\)-adic valuation on \(\mathbb Q_p\), so that \(v_p(p)=1\) and \(|x|_p=p^{-v_p(x)}\) for \(x\ne0\). Recall that \(v_p(x)\in\mathbb Z\) for every nonzero \(x\in\mathbb Q_p\), and that
\[
\mathbb Z_p=\{x\in\mathbb Q_p:|x|_p\le1\}=\{0\}\cup\{x\in\mathbb Q_p:v_p(x)\ge0\}.
\]
The ultrametric inequality and multiplicativity of the norm show that this set is closed under addition and multiplication; it also contains \(0,1\) and is closed under additive inverses. Thus \(\mathbb Z_p\) is a commutative ring.

We first identify the ideal \(p\mathbb Z_p\). If \(z\in\mathbb Z_p\), then
\[
|pz|_p=|p|_p|z|_p=p^{-1}|z|_p<1
\]
when \(z\ne0\), and the same conclusion is immediate when \(z=0\). Hence every element of \(p\mathbb Z_p\) has norm less than \(1\). Conversely, suppose \(x\in\mathbb Z_p\) and \(|x|_p<1\). If \(x=0\), then certainly \(x\in p\mathbb Z_p\). If \(x\ne0\), then \(v_p(x)>0\). Since \(v_p(x)\) is an integer, \(v_p(x)\ge1\), and therefore
\[
v_p(x/p)=v_p(x)-1\ge0.
\]
Thus \(x/p\in\mathbb Z_p\), so \(x=p(x/p)\in p\mathbb Z_p\). Consequently,
\[
p\mathbb Z_p=\{x\in\mathbb Z_p:|x|_p<1\}. \tag{1}
\]

We next determine the units of \(\mathbb Z_p\). If \(x\in\mathbb Z_p\) satisfies \(|x|_p=1\), then \(|x^{-1}|_p=|x|_p^{-1}=1\), so \(x^{-1}\in\mathbb Z_p\); hence \(x\) is a unit. On the other hand, if \(|x|_p<1\), then for every \(y\in\mathbb Z_p\) one has
\[
|xy|_p=|x|_p|y|_p<1,
\]
so \(xy\ne1\). Thus \(x\) is not a unit. By (1), the nonunits of \(\mathbb Z_p\) are exactly the elements of \(p\mathbb Z_p\).

The ideal \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is proper, since \(1\notin p\mathbb Z_p\). If an ideal \(I\) properly contains \(p\mathbb Z_p\), choose \(a\in I\setminus p\mathbb Z_p\). Then \(a\) is a unit by the preceding characterization, so \(1=a^{-1}a\in I\), and hence \(I=\mathbb Z_p\). Therefore \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is maximal. Finally, if \(M\) is any maximal ideal of \(\mathbb Z_p\), then no element of \(M\) can be a unit. Hence every element of \(M\) belongs to \(p\mathbb Z_p\), so \(M\subseteq p\mathbb Z_p\). Since \(M\) is maximal and \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is a proper ideal, it follows that \(M=p\mathbb Z_p\). Thus \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is the unique maximal ideal of \(\mathbb Z_p\), and consequently \(\mathbb Z_p\) is a local ring.
